page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs operating on 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache. The system is provisioned with 8 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It includes zero bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for persistence.

Performance profiles demonstrate pronounced single-thread strength. The instance achieves a top-quartile result in stress-ng single-core testing at 2924.48, alongside moderate single-core Geekbench performance of 1649.0. However, the four-thread envelope limits parallel scaling, placing stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics in the lower quartiles. Memory bandwidth yields typical uncached sequential transfers of 44.87 GB/sec read and 28.8 GB/sec write, though the overall PassMark memory score reflects lower efficiency relative to larger memory configurations.

This hardware footprint functions as an efficient compute-centric tier for workloads that do not demand expansive memory footprints. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs reduces resource overhead, maintaining dedicated CPU performance. Appropriate workload targets include continuous integration runners, lightweight compilation, stateless web microservices, and small batch jobs that depend on stable per-thread throughput.
